lesson_title: Number Patterns: The Can Pyramid Question
hook_text: 7 rows of cans. Matrics answered 7. The paper wanted 28. Here's the difference.
clip_script: Picture the pyramid of cans at the supermarket entrance. One can on top. Two in the row below. Then three, then four — every row one can wider than the row above. Seven rows down, the display is done. How many cans were carried from the storeroom? Say it as you build: one. Plus two, three. Plus three, six. Plus four, ten. Plus five, fifteen. Plus six, twenty-one. Plus seven, twenty-eight. The seventh row holds 7 cans, but the display holds 28 — read what the question counts.
visual_style: Stop-motion can pyramid assembling row by row with a running counter ticking up, freezing on 7 versus 28 side by side.
pacing: Rhythmic build with the counter, beat of silence, punchline lands on 28.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and never lose the stacked-rows marks again.
